exec: Sustained law-enforcement pressure on dark web markets, with large asset seizures and investigations still running.
plain: Police in 14 countries, coordinated by Europol, arrested 354 people who sold or bought illegal goods on hidden online markets and seized about five tonnes of drugs and over 210 million euros.

key_findings: Operation TorNado ran from May 2025 to October 2026 across 14 countries and led to 354 arrests and hundreds of house searches.
It identified vendors and buyers after the takedown of five dark markets: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door.
Arrests were highest in the United States (132), United Kingdom (59), Hungary (45) and Germany (41).
Seizures: 950 kg of drugs and over EUR 60 million in Europe; over 4.8 tonnes of drugs, 152 firearms and over EUR 150 million in the United States.
Europol notes markets are fragmenting, blending with encrypted messaging services, and being replaced quickly after takedowns.
recommendations: The release gives no guidance for organisations or the public.

summary: Europol says Operation TorNado, run with law enforcement from 14 countries between May 2025 and October 2026, led to 354 arrests of dark web vendors and buyers, 132 of them in the United States and 59 in the United Kingdom. It followed the takedown of five markets: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. About five tonnes of drugs, 209 firearms and more than EUR 210 million were seized.
title: Europol: Operation TorNado dark web crackdown nets 354 arrests in 14-country action
